newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - IFC brings first peso Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - IFC brings first peso Eurobond.

text.p: The International Finance Corp's launching of the first-ever Philippine peso Eurobond was the highlight of Asian debt markets on Monday.
The 2.6 billion peso bond matures in five years and carries a coupon of 10.25 percent. Citicorp International is lead manager for the issue.
Investors that buy the bond assume Philippine currency risk but not credit risk because the bond carries the AAA rating of the IFC, which is the investment arm of the World Bank.
Citicorp said that the dollar amount of the bond is US$98,821,741 using a set exchange rate of 26.3099 pesos per U.S. dollar.
Fees total 60 basis points, split as 25 basis points for selling and 35 basis points for management and underwriting.
Denominations are 1.0 million and 5.0 million pesos.
Andrew Alcid, director of debt syndications at Citicorp in Manila, said the issue is attracting interest from emerging market fund managers.
"It's mostly fund managers that are comfortable with the Philippine currency and some of them have actually bought Philippine government securities in the past," said Alcid.
Citicorp expects most of the demand for the issue to come from Asia, he said.
"We're projecting anywhere from 65 to 75 percent will go to Asian accounts and then the balance will be split between Europe and the U.S.," said Alcid.
But he said it is still too early to assess demand from Europe and the U.S.
The bond will be priced during Asian hours on Tuesday.
The Philippines also has approved a peso-denominated bond by the World Bank to be lead managed by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Hong Kong borrowers also were in the news.
HSBC Investing Bank said that it has launched a HK$3.5 billion term loan for Hong Kong Electric.
The loan is split evenly between two tranches. Both mature in seven years but tranche A can be put after five years, while tranche B has no put options.
Bankers said tranche A pays an all-in return in the low 40s over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate, while tranche B pays an all-in return in the mid 40s.
Some local bankers complained the pricing is too tight, but the issue is expected to attract demand from Japanese banks that have a relationship with the borrower.
Henderson Land also is seen in the market with a five-year revolving credit that pays an all-in return of 57 basis points.
As expected, there are more floating rate certificate of deposit issues in the offing that will qualify for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
Chekiang First Bank, a wholly owned unit of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank, reportedly is seeking a HK$1.0 billion FRCD, its first LAF-eligible deal. Chekiang has been rated A-plus by IBCA.
Bankers said Bank of East Asia also is considering a LAF issue.
Elsewhere, Hanil Bank has launched a 300 million mark three-year bond through lead manager Bayerische Landesbank.
The 4.375 percent bond was launched at 101.235 and re-offered at 99.66 to yield 51 basis points over comparable German government bonds.
